requirements.requirement: Configure node1 so the kernel boots with audit=1 and the setting persists across reboots.
requirements.summary: Before the change, the live command line and boot entries lacked audit=1. The executor added exactly one audit=1 to every boot entry, performed a bounded reboot, observed a new boot identity, and then directly verified exactly one live audit=1, kernel auditing enabled, and persistent audit=1 in all entries and GRUB defaults.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged across the work and reboot. The change used the platform-installed, RPM-owned RHEL grubby utility; no replacement OS, kernel, or third-party software installation is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 demonstrably rebooted from boot ID 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72 to a57b9526-59ef-4b0b-9e75-7a592fb44ae3, returned with audit=1 active and persistent, and retained its RHEL release and installed kernel. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-state, acknowledged restart, observed interruption, changed boot identity, and recovered services, access, protected-data checksums, and failed-unit state were captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were observed. The grubby update was directly required for persistent audit=1 (cmd-68f9ad7f8f704cdc), and the scheduled reboot was required both to prove boot persistence and to satisfy the provider restart protocol (cmd-a7e51d859510494c). Its transient systemd units were automatically removed after reboot, with cleanup verified (cmd-e82aa323253a455f). Final observations show no failed services, no unwanted socket exposure, healthy package state, and only expected reboot-related temporary-file/PID changes.
